content: The dual of a triangulation is defined by joining the centroids of adjacent triangles. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dual_graph

title: Kerner
content: Classic reference: Immo Kerner, Ein Gesamtschrittverfahren zur Berechnung der Nullstellen von Polynomen, 1966. The Durand-Kerner method is surprisingly simple way of computing all the roots of a polynomial. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Durand%E2%80%93Kerner_method

title: Aliasing
content: Sampling a signal is equivalent to periodizing its Fourier transform. For non-smooth signals (with non-compact Fourier transform), it creates aliazing. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nyquist%E2%80%93Shannon_sampling_theorem

title: Fp Sampling
content: The farthest point sampling is a greedy algorithm which asymptotically samples from a uniform density defined by a distance (e.g. geodesic). Defines a Delone set. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Farthest-first_traversal https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Delone_set

title: Monge
content: Gaspard Monge proved in 1781 that optimal assignment for the Euclidean cost can never cross. https://fr.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gaspard_Monge http://images.math.cnrs.fr/Gaspard-Monge,1094.html

title: Muntz
content: Muntz-Szasz theorem gives a sharp condition for lacunary polynomials to be dense. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/M%C3%BCntz%E2%80%93Sz%C3%A1sz_theorem

title: Boltzmann
content: Classic reference: L. Boltzmann, Weitere studien über das Wärmegleichgewicht unter Gasmolekülen, 1872. Boltzmann transport equation describes the mean field limit of a growing number of evolving particles with a decreasing radius. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boltzmann_equation

title: Haar
content: Non-linear approximation in a Haar wavelets basis performs an adaptive approximation on a dyadic partition. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Haar_wavelet

title: Foveation
content: Foveation is a spatially varying "convolution". https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Foveated_imaging https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Retina

title: Barron
content: Multilayer perceptrons with 1 hidden layer approximate functions using sums of ridge functions. Approximation rates have been stated by Andrew Barron. http://www.stat.yale.edu/~arb4/publications_files/UniversalApproximationBoundsForSuperpositionsOfASigmoidalFunction.pdf

title: Wigner Ville
content: The Wigner-Ville distribution mimics a probability distribution on the space-frequency plane. Useful to define the instantaneous frequency of a signal as the conditional expectation of frequencies. Suffers from interferences. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wigner_distribution_function

title: Kubo Ando
content: Classic reference: F Kubo and T Ando, Means of Positive Linear Operators, 1980, The Kubo-Ando mean generalizes geometric mean to matrices and preserves key properties (e.g. concavity and arithmetic-geometric inequality). https://link.springer.com/content/pdf/10.1007/BF01371042.pdf

title: Ot Interp Gaussians
content: The Optimal Transport interpolation between two Gaussians is a Gaussian.

title: Implicit Euler
content: Gradient flows on metric spaces: define descent methods on non-Euclidean domains without using a gradient. A key tool studied in details by Ambrosio, Gigli and Savare. http://www.springer.com/la/book/9783764387211

title: Kl Ot
content: Geometry of Gaussians: Optimal Transport is flat (Euclidean) while Fisher-Rao is hyperbolic (Poincare half-plane). https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fisher_information_metric

title: Lasso
content: L2 (ridge) vs L1 (lasso) are used for the regularization of regression problems. L1 induces a sparsity prior and correctly recovers isolated spikes even with correlated designs. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tikhonov_regularization https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lasso_(statistics)

title: Cfl
content: The Courant-Friedrichs-Lewy (CFL) condition relates time/space step sizes for the stability of finite difference methods. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Courant%E2%80%93Friedrichs%E2%80%93Lewy_condition

title: Motzkin
content: Positive 1D polynomials are sums of squares. Motzkin's 2D polynomial is positive but is not a sum of squares. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Positive_polynomial https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sum-of-squares_optimization

title: Automata
content: Cellular automata are discrete dynamical models defined by a local operator. For 3 neighbors automata, there are 256 possible rules, some more interesting than others. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cellular_automaton

title: Fourier Cat
content: Fourier approximation of a cat. https://xkcd.com/26/

title: Burger
content: Burgers' equation is one of the simplest nonlinear partial differential equations, with solutions exhibiting shocks. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burgers%27_equation

title: Metaballs
content: "Metaballs" are levelsets of mixtures of radial basis functions, which generate blobby lava-lamp-like behaviors. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metaballs https://fr.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Blinn https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lava_lamp

title: Interpolations
content: Comparing 2D linear interpolation methods of order 0, 1 and 3. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Multivariate_interpolation

title: Gauss Mixtures
content: A mixture of Gaussians can be represented as a weighted points cloud (actually a measure) over the mean/covariance domain. Mixture fitting is a non-convex optimization problem. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mixture_model

title: Tsp
content: The Travelling salesman problem is one of the most well known NP-hard problem. Concorde's solver can be used to solve exactly or approximately even large instances. http://www.math.uwaterloo.ca/tsp/index.html

title: Schrodinger
content: Schrodinger's problem is an approximation (regularization using diffusion) of the Optimal Transport problem. https://arxiv.org/abs/1308.0215

title: Harris
content: Harris's method is the most frequently used corner detector, based on the eigenvalues of the structure tensor. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harris_Corner_Detector

title: Fixedpoints
content: Fixed points can be attractive or repulsive depending on the derivative of the map. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fixed_point_(mathematics)

title: Heat Diff
content: Adding an independent Gaussian variable is the same as doing a heat diffusion on the density. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Convolution_of_probability_distributions

title: Icp
content: Iterative closest point is one of the basic algorithms for rigid shape registration. Leverages the closed form formula of least square rigid motion. Can be coupled with optimal transport (e.g. Hungarian algorithm). https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iterative_closest_point

title: Mlp
content: Training a multilayer perceptron with a single hidden layer corresponds to the evolution of a sparse probability measure (sum of Dirac masses) over the neuron's parameter domain (here it is 2D for the regression of a 1D function, slope+position of the ridge). Useful analogy to understand the mean-field limit of an i...

title: Pinsker
content: Pinsker's inequality is a fundamental inequality of information theory. Bounds the total variation norm by the relative entropy (also known as KL divergence). https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pinsker%27s_inequality

title: Tv Denoise
content: Total variation denoising (Leonid Rudin, Stanley Osher, Emad Fatemi, 92) was studied in theory among others by Vicent Caselles. He proved (with collaborators including Antonin Chambolle) that it does not create discontinuities but blurs corners. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Total_variation_denoising

title: Sdp Optim
content: One can encode or approximate convex shapes as intersections of the semi-definite positive cone and affine spaces (linear matrix inequalities). This allows one to use interior point methods to solve optimization on these sets. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Linear_matrix_inequality

title: De Boor
content: Non-uniform B-splines functions are smooth piecewise polynomial functions, which can be generalized to rational functions by weighting (NURBS). The backbone of computer aided geometric design and extensively used in computer graphics. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Non-uniform_rational_B-spline

title: Qr
content: The QR decomposition can be computed in a numerically stable way using planar rotation matrices. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Givens_rotation

title: Svd
content: The SVD decomposes the action of a matrix into rotations and scalings along the axes. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Singular_value_decomposition

title: Monotone
content: Monotone operators (Minty, Browder) generalize monotone functions. (sub)-gradients of convex functions are (maximal) monotone. Skew-symmetric (gradients of min-max) operators are also monotone. These are the two extremal cases (Asplund). https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Monotonic_function

title: Weierstrass
content: The Weierstrass function is continuous if a<1 but nowhere differentiable if ab 1. The Hausdorff dimension of its graph was conjectured by Mandelbrot in 1977 and proved by Shen in 2016. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Weierstrass_function https://arxiv.org/abs/1505.03986

title: Reaction Diffusion
content: Reaction-diffusions are nonlinear PDEs which describe the formation of a surprisingly rich family of patterns. Introduced by Alan Turing in 1952. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reaction%E2%80%93diffusion_system http://www.dna.caltech.edu/courses/cs191/paperscs191/turing.pdf

title: Rkhs 001
content: Reproducing Kernel Hilbert spaces define norms on functions so that solutions of regularized fitting problems are linear sum of kernel functions. Defines non-parametric learning methods (complexity scales with input). https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reproducing_kernel_Hilbert_space

title: Ot Gaussians
content: The Optimal Transport geometry of 1-D Gaussians is flat in the (mean, std) plane. In particular, the OT interpolation is a linear interpolation of mean and std.

title: Bifurcation
content: Polynomial maps exhibit bifurcations and chaotic behavior for some values of their coefficients. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Logistic_map

title: Medial 001
content: The medial axis (also known as the skeleton) generalizes the mediatrix between two points. It is the set of points where the distance function is not smooth. It is the set of points that have two equi-spaced closed points. For discrete points, delimitates the Voronoi diagrams. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Medial_ax...

title: Bernstein
content: Bernstein polynomials can be used to approximate 1D functions but also 2D curves (corresponding to Bezier curves). https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bernstein_polynomial

title: Step Size
content: Step size selection is important for gradient descent on ill-conditioned functions.

title: W1 Graphs 001
content: The Wasserstein-1 distance (which is a norm! ) between histograms on graphs is equivalent to a min-cost flow. Bold black indicates edges where mass is flowing. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Minimum-cost_flow_problem

title: Banach Fixed Point
content: Banach fixed point theorem ensures existence of a unique fixed point for contracting maps. The proof is constructive by iterating the map. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Banach_fixed-point_theorem

title: Parabolic Hyperbolic
content: Parabolic PDEs (e.g. heat) smooth out singularities. Hyperbolic PDEs (e.g. wave) displace singularities. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heat_equation https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wave_equation https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parabolic_partial_differential_equation https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hyperbolic_partial_diffe...

title: Qr
content: The QR decomposition can be computed in a numerically stable way using reflection matrices. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Householder_transformation

title: Divergences
content: Csiszar divergences is a unifying way to define losses between arbitrary positive measures (discrete & densities). https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/F-divergence https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0209021

title: Step Size
content: "Greedy" gradient descent using optimal step choice at each iteration produces orthogonal successive directions. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gradient_descent

title: Heat
content: The heat can be applied to diffuse probability density (in particular, maintains positivity and unit mass). It corresponds to the distribution of a Brownian motion at time t. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heat_equation

title: Lloyd
content: Loyds algorithm defines a segmentation of the domain using Voronoi cells. The associated dual graph is a Delaunay triangulation. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lloyd%27s_algorithm

title: Harmonic
content: Harmonic functions are obtained by solving Laplace equation and define interpolating functions when using Dirichlet boundary conditions. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laplace%27s_equation

title: Fft
content: The Fast Fourier and Wavelet transforms correspond to two sparse factorizations of an orthonormal matrix, leading to two fast iterative algorithms of O(n log(n)) and O(n) complexities. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fast_Fourier_transform https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Haar_wavelet

title: Pendulum
content: The simple gravity pendulum is one of the simplest nonlinear second order ODE. Exhibits elliptic-shape orbits in phase space for small enough initial speeds. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pendulum_(mathematics)

title: Taylor Exp
content: Taylor series approximate within its radius of convergence a function by a polynomial. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_series

title: Power Method
content: Power iterations converge to the leading eigenvector of a matrix. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Power_iteration

title: Advection
content: Diffeomorphisms (warpings) are conveniently described in a Lagrangian way by advecting particles along a flow field. The Eulerian description corresponds to the advection equation. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Advection https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diffeomorphism https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagrangian_mechanics

title: Nurbs
content: Rational Bezier curves generalize Bernstein approximation using weights. Enables the approximation of arbitrary quadric (such as circles). https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Non-uniform_rational_B-spline

title: Roots Poly
content: Interpolating linearly polynomials of a fixed degree defines an interpolation between their roots. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vieta%27s_formulas

title: Flattening
content: One can map a surface to a sphere by minimizing a Dirichlet energy. https://www.numerical-tours.com/matlab/meshdeform_2_parameterization_sphere

title: Gauss Luca
content: Gauss-Luca theorem shows that the roots of the derivative of a polynomial belong to the convex hull of the roots of the polynomial. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gauss%E2%80%93Lucas_theorem

title: Lloyd
content: Lloyd algorithm can be used to progressively diffuse points, defining a dynamical system over distributions. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lloyd%27s_algorithm

title: Legendre Fast
content: The Legendre transform can be approximated in O(n log(n)) using a Gaussian convolution. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Legendre_transformation https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lower_convex_envelope

title: Marching Cube
content: The marching squares/cubes is the standard algorithm to extract iso-curves/surfaces from a discretized image/volume. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marching_squares https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marching_cubes

title: Marden Thm
content: Marden theorem states that the roots of P'' are the focal point of the Steiner ellipse (largest enclosed ellipse in area) of the triangle formed by the roots of P. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marden%27s_theorem

title: Divergence Dual Norm
content: Comparing probability distributions: Csiszar f-divergences measure "vertical" displacement of mass, whereas dual norm of smooth functions rather measure "horizontal" displacements. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/F-divergence

title: Spectral Lifting
content: Reasonable properties (convexity, differentiability, stratifiability, partial-smoothness...) lift from vectors to matrices! https://people.orie.cornell.edu/aslewis/publications/03-mathematics.pdf

title: Delaunay Hull
content: The Delaunay triangulation in d dimensions can be obtained by computing the convex hull on a paraboloid lifting in d+1 dimensions. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Delaunay_triangulation#d-dimensional_Delaunay

title: Game Life
content: The Game of Life is a well-known 2D cellular automaton. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conway%27s_Game_of_Life

title: Krigging
content: Kriging (also known as Wiener interpolation) is a method for kernel interpolation that accounts for uncertainty using Gaussian processes. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kriging

title: L1 Norm
content: The l1 norm provides an optimal balance between convexity and sparsity. It is used in various applications including the lasso and basis pursuit denoising, pioneered by David Donoho and Robert Tibshirani. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Basis_pursuit_denoising, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lasso_(statistics)

title: Mesh Compression
content: This video demonstrates progressive decompression of a 3D mesh. http://www.cs.technion.ac.il/~gotsman/AmendedPubl/SpectralCompression/SpectralCompression.pdf

title: Oscillator
content: The harmonic oscillator is the canonical linear second order ODE. Parametrized by a single damping parameter. Solutions are (possibly complex) exponentials. Interpolates between periodic motion and exponential decay. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harmonic_oscillator

title: Voltera Lotka
content: Lotka-Volterra equations is a non-linear 2D ODE modeling prey/predator behaviors which exhibits periodic solutions. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lotka%E2%80%93Volterra_equations

title: Heavy Ball
content: Poljak heavy ball method speeds up gradient descent by introducing momentum. Corresponding to second order ODEs. https://distill.pub/2017/momentum/

title: Periodic Motions
content: Only harmonic spring and gravity central forces produce periodic motions. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bertrand%27s_theorem

title: Kernel Domain
content: The kernel of a domain is the (convex) set of locations from which you can see all other locations in the domain. It is the intersections of all half-planes tangent to the shape. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Star-shaped_polygon

title: John Ellipsoid
content: John's and Lowner's ellipsoids are polar one from each others. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_ellipsoid

title: Sobolev Ball
content: A Sobolev ball is an ellipsoid in infinite dimension aligned along the Fourier axes. A random Sobolev function has a Fourier transform with random phase. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sobolev_space

title: Denoising Flows
content: The gradient flow of the Dirichlet energy is the heat equation, which blur edges. The total variation flow makes the image cartoon-like, and requires some care to be defined and implemented (division by 0 when the gradient vanishes). https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heat_equation https://www.uv.es/mazon/trabajos/DIE.pd...

title: Co Area
content: The co-area formula relates the total variation to the perimeters of the level set. Can be extended to (possibly) discontinuous functions of bounded total variation. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coarea_formula

title: Logistic Map
content: The logistic map can have complex patterns of adherence points depending on the value of its scale parameter r. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Logistic_map

title: Helmoltz Decomposition
content: The Helmholtz-Hodge decomposition split vectors fields in two orthogonal subspaces: incompressible and irrotational. In 2-D, corresponds to the sum of a gradient field and a rotated gradient field. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Helmholtz_decomposition

title: Mean Shift
content: The mean-shift algorithm is a clustering method that progressively evolves points toward local maximum of a kernel density estimator. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mean_shift

title: Daubechies
content: Daubechies wavelets is a parametric family of orthogonal Wavelets. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daubechies_wavelet https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ingrid_Daubechies

title: Nestero Polyak
content: Poljak heavy ball and Nesterov methods speed up gradient descent by introducing momentum. Corresponding to second order ODEs. https://distill.pub/2017/momentum/

title: Dual Numbers
content: Dual number is a convenient way to implement forward mode of automatic differentiation. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dual_number

title: Interpolation Grids
content: Impact of the interpolation method on the level set of the resulting function. https://fr.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marching_cubes https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Level_set

title: Thin Plate
content: Thin plate spline is one of the most popular data interpolation methods. Its solution can be written in 2D using the r^2 log(r) radial basis function. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thin_plate_spline#cite_note-Duchon76-1

title: Discretization Measure
content: Lagrangian discretization of measures: quotient space. Eulerian discretization: convex polytope.

title: Pendulum Oscilator
content: The damped harmonic oscillator (linear) vs simple gravity pendulum (non-linear). The two most celebrated second order dynamical systems. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harmonic_oscillator https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pendulum_(mathematics)#Simple_gravity_pendulum

title: Iterative Projections
content: Iterative projections: converge in theory for convex sets. Works great in practice for non-convex sets. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Projections_onto_convex_sets

title: Proximal Operator
content: The proximal operator is the implicit counterpart of the explicit gradient descent step. Fundamental to tackle non-smooth optimization problems. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Proximal_operator

title: Sgd
content: Stochastic gradient method: works also for infinite sums and expectation. Introduced by Herbert Robbins and Sutton Monro. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stochastic_approximation https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stochastic_gradient_descent

title: Aniso Diffusion
content: Tensor-driven anisotropic diffusion solves the heat equation on a manifold defined by a tensor field. At the heart of many methods for image restauration, texture enhancement and vizualization. The book of Joachim Weickert is a must read. https://www.mia.uni-saarland.de/weickert/Papers/book.pdf

title: Power Iter Convergence
content: Power iterations do not converge for matrices with multiple complex eigenvalues with same maximum modulus. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Power_iteration

title: Knn
content: K-nearest neighbors is the baseline method for non-parametric classification. Computes an estimate of the relative density of the two classes. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/K-nearest_neighbors_algorithm

title: Leapfrog
content: Leapfrog/Verlet are symplectic integrators which approximately conserve hamiltonian, preserve periodic behaviors and are exactly reversible. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leapfrog_integration https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Verlet_integration

title: Taylor Exp
content: Taylor series of exp(it) up to degree 15. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_series

title: Heat Eq
content: The heat equation can be applied to diffuse probability densities (in particular, maintains positivity and unit mass). Its solution is obtained as the convolution of the initial condition with a Gaussian. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heat_equation

title: Binomial
content: The binomial law is a sum of Bernoulli 0/1 random variables. After rescaling, converge to a Gaussian for a large number of variables (a particular case of the central limit theorem). https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Binomial_distribution

title: Convex Hull
content: The convex hull is the smallest enclosing convex set. It is also the intersection of all half-spaces containing the points, and the set of all possible convex combinations. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Convex_hull

title: Lin Dyn Systems
content: Behavior of dynamical system depends on the eigenvalues. In 2D it can be classified according to the trace and determinant. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stability_theory https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Linear_dynamical_system

title: Self Org Maps
content: Self-organizing maps of Kohonen defines a map between a 2D space to the data, by minimizing a quantization error and a regularity penalty. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Self-organizing_map

title: Rbf
content: Radial basis functions performs interpolation and approximation by solving a linear system. In some cases (e.g. Gaussian and polyharmonic), corresponds to regression in a reproducing Hilbert space. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Radial_basis_function

title: Lorentz Attractor
content: Lorenz attractor is the set of limit trajectories for a simplified mathematical model for atmospheric convection. It has a fractal geometry. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lorenz_system

title: Huffman Code
content: Code words defined using a Huffman tree generate codes with optimal average length. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Huffman_coding https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=JsTptu56GM8&t=310s

title: Penrose Tiling
content: Penrose tiling are aperiodic tilings obtained using typically 2 isosceles triangles with two type of edge labelings (so 4 types of triangles). A way to generate the tiling is by applying iterative edge splitting using the golden ratio. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Penrose_tiling https://github.com/mathworks/penrose...

title: Heat Surf
content: The heat equation can be applied on a surface and to a surface. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laplace%E2%80%93Beltrami_operator

title: Line Int Conv
content: Line integral convolution is an anisotropic filtering which averages values along streamlines. Can be used for vizualization of vector fields by diffusing noise. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Line_integral_convolution

title: Entropy Estimators
content: Summing the log of the nearest neighbors distances: a simple estimator for the entropy from samples. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Entropy_estimation

title: Frac Derivative
content: The fractional Laplacian is a differential operator generalizing the Laplacian. They are the only rotation/translation/scale invariant linear operator. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fractional_Laplacian

title: Mp Random Matrices
content: The Marchenko-Pastur law is the distribution limit of eigenvalues of covariance matrices when samples and size grow together. http://djalil.chafai.net/blog/2011/01/29/the-marchenko-pastur-

title: Lin Nonlin Approx
content: Linear approximation selects the first coefficients of a decomposition in an orthogonal basis. Non-linear selects the best coefficients. Non-linear approximation in a Wavelet basis is efficient to handle non-smooth functions. http://people.math.sc.edu/devore/publications/NLACTA.pdf

title: Varadhan Formula
content: Varadhan formula shows that at first order, the heat kernel is equal to the geodesic kernel. They are exactly equal on Euclidean spaces. http://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1002/cpa.3160200210/abstract

title: Tutte Embedding
content: Tutte theorem defines a valid drawing of planar graphs by solving a linear system. A fundamental tool to compute surface parameterization. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tutte_embedding http://nbviewer.jupyter.org/github/gpeyre/numerical-tours/blob/master/python/meshdeform_1_parameterization.ipynb

title: Verlet
content: Stormer, Verlet and leapfrog are different names for the same method. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leapfrog_integration https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Verlet_integration

title: Taylor Sine
content: Taylor series expansion of sine. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_series

title: L1 Highdim
content: Vitali Milman's insight: convex sets in high dimension look like hedgehogs http://www.math.tau.ac.il/~milman/files/survey4.ps

title: Gromov Haus
content: The space of metric spaces is a metric space for the Gromov-Hausdorff distance. Important tool to study convergence of spaces. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gromov%E2%80%93Hausdorff_convergence

title: Computation Graph
content: Implementing a numerical function corresponds to the creation of a directed acyclic graph and operating a topological sorting of its nodes. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Directed_acyclic_graph

title: Manifold Optim
content: Optimization can be carried over on manifolds using gradient descent, where the manifold gradient is the projection of an extrinsic gradient on the tangent plane. https://sites.uclouvain.be/absil/amsbook/

title: Mid Points Drawing
content: Iteratively joining the mid points of the edges of a polygon converges toward the centroids of its vertices.

title: Moebius
content: A sub-group of Mobius transforms are those preserving the Poincare upper-half (equivalently the disk). It corresponds to PSL(2) the 2x2 matrices with determinant 1. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/M%C3%B6bius_transformation#Subgroups_of_the_M%C3%B6bius_group

title: Tomography
content: Filtered back-propagation is a formula for the invert of the Radon transform, which can be approximated by using a finite of Radon projections. The basic method to reconstruct images in scanner imaging. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tomographic_reconstruction

title: Random Matrix
content: Eigenvalues of random matrices with iid entries converge to the Wigner circle law. This is universal (does not depend on the law of the entries), as proved by Tao and Vu in 2010. For Gaussian matrices, this defines a determinental point process. https://arxiv.org/abs/0908.1982 https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Circular_law

title: Cizar
content: Csiszar divergences compare the relative distributions of two histograms with 1. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/F-divergence

title: Heat Crossings
content: Zero crossing of the derivative of a blurred version (heat diffusion) of a function defines the so-called scale space representation. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scale_space

title: Wasserstein Hellinger
content: Comparison of the Wasserstein, Hellinger, Kullback-Leibler and reverse KL on the space of Gaussian distributions. http://djalil.chafai.net/blog/2020/01/22/about-the-hellinger-distance/

title: Fermat Torricelli
content: The Fermat-Torricelli point minimizes the sum of the distance to the vertices of a triangle. If the angles are less than 120°, can be computed by forming three equilateral triangles, otherwise it is one of the vertices. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fermat_point

title: Dct
content: Discrete Cosine Transforms are eigenvectors of Laplacians with different boundary conditions. Wonderful paper by Strang. http://www-math.mit.edu/~gs/papers/dct.pdf

title: Brownian
content: A Brownian motion is approximated by a discrete random walk with Gaussian increments. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brownian_motion

title: Shatten Norms
content: Schatten p-norms are the l^p norms of the singular values. Define algebra norm invariant by isometries. Generalizes the nuclear norm (p=1), Frobenius norm (p=2) and the operator norm (p=inf). https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Schatten_norm

title: Reeb Graph
content: The Reeb graph of a function on a manifold is the graph of level sets ordered by inclusion. For a 2D function (an image), it is the contour graph, and is actually a directed tree (polytree). https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reeb_graph https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Polytree

title: Fourier Legendre
content: Fourier is to convolution what Legendre is to inf-convolution. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fourier_transform https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Legendre_transformation

title: Perceptron
content: A 1 hidden layer perceptron can approximate arbitrary continuous functions using a large enough number of neurons (Cybenko's theorem). https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Universal_approximation_theorem https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Multilayer_perceptron

title: Subdiff
content: The subdifferential is the set of slopes bellow the graph of a convex function. It is a set-valued monotone map. Generalize the gradient to non-smooth functions. The most fundamental tool of non-smooth convex analysis. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Subderivative

title: Eikonale
content: The distance field is the unique viscosity solution of the Eikonale equation. Pierre-Louis Lions got the Fields medal in 1994 in part for this concept. https://projecteuclid.org/euclid.jmsj/1230130200 http://nbviewer.jupyter.org/github/gpeyre/numerical-tours/blob/master/python/fastmarching_0_implementing.ipynb

title: Triangulation Images
content: Approximation using anisotropic triangulations performs optimal compression of cartoon images. Finding the optimal triangulation is intractable, heuristics are used in practice. Wavelets are suboptimal, but still very much used because of linear time algorithms. The PhD thesis of Jean-Marie Mirebeau is a fantastic s...

title: Visual Cortex
content: The primary visual cortex is organised as an oriented wavelet transform. Huber and Wiesel got the Nobel prize for this discovery. Mapping the orientation on the surface of the cortex creates singularities called pinwheells. The 2003 special issue of J Phys Paris on Neurogeometry still very inspiring. https://www.sci...

title: Flow Manifold
content: The integral curves of a vector field tangent to a manifold stays on the manifold. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Integral_curve

title: Manifold
content: A Riemannian manifold is locally an Euclidean space. An embedded surface (e.g. the Earth) is an example. It defines a Riemannian tensors field (first fundamental form) in parametric space which encode length deformations. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Riemannian_manifold https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parametric_surf...

title: Mean Curvature
content: The mean curvature motion is the most fundamental curve evolution. It is the equivalent for curves of the heat equation. It is independent of parameterisation (intrinsic) and minimizes the length of the curve (shortening flow). It shrinks the curves toward an ellipse. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Curve-shortening_f...

title: Backprop
content: Reverse mode automatic-differentiation is based on a "backward" (adjoint) chain rule. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Automatic_differentiation#Reverse_accumulation

title: Fourier Periodization
content: Fourier transforms comes with lots of flavors. Sampling and periodization are dual operations which interleave these transforms. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fourier_transform

title: Continued Fraction
content: Continued fractions are in some sense optimal ways to approximate with rational numbers. Expansion of rational are finite. Expansion of quadratic numbers are periodic. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Continued_fraction

title: Brownian Evol
content: The average distance to origin of a Brownian motion at time t grows like sqrt(t). https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brownian_motion

title: Projections
content: Curse and blessing of non-smooth optimization: non-smooth parts (eg corners of sets) attract the solutions of optimization problems (e.g. projection on sets). https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Subderivative https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Variational_analysis

title: Median Vs Mean
content: Minimizing sum of p-powers of the distance generalizes the mean (p=2). For p=1, one obtains the median which is robust to outliers. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Geometric_median

title: Nmf Pca
content: Principal component analysis and non-negative matrix factorization are two particular of non-convex matrix factorization problem. They differ by the constraints on the atoms D and coefficients X. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Principal_component_analysis https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Non-negative_matrix_factorization

title: Gears
content: Non-circular gears generate non-regular motions from regular one. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Non-circular_gear

title: Inverse Kin
content: The Levenberg-Marquardt is a standard method for non-linear least-squares, combining the best of gradient descent and Newton methods by replacing the Hessian by the Jacobian term only. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Levenberg%E2%80%93Marquardt_algorithm

title: Pinsker
content: Pinsker inequality is one of the most fundamental inequality in information theory. Upper bounds the total variation (i.e. l^1 norm) by the square root of the relative entropy (i.e. the Kullback-Leibler divergence). https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pinsker%27s_inequality

title: Binary Cube
content: Error checking code with an additional parity bit defines a simplex in the binary cube. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parity_bit

title: Ellastic Net
content: Elastic net (Zou, Hastie, 2005) interpolates between the Lasso (l1 regularization) and Ridge regression (l2 regularization). The regularization path of Lasso is polygonal. The one of elastic net is piecewise smooth. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elastic_net_regularization http://nbviewer.jupyter.org/github/gpeyre/nu...

title: Geodesic Distance
content: The geodesic distance extends a local metric into a global one. Geodesic curves define networks of curves that are similar to spanning trees on a graph. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Geodesic https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Riemannian_manifold

title: Wass Hellinger Gauss
content: The Wasserstein and Hellinger distances between Gaussians can be computed in closed form. http://djalil.chafai.net/blog/2020/01/22/about-the-hellinger-distance/

title: Newton Fractal
content: Understanding global convergence of Newton method is hard. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Newton_fractal

title: Shapiro Ineq
content: Shapiro's inequality: for small integers, cyclic sums of quotients is always larger than n/2, which corresponds to x=(1, ..., 1), being the only local minimum with non zero entries. For large n, it only gets strictly smaller by 1% (by zeroing non consecutive entries of x). https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shapiro_inequ...

title: Fourier Non Com
content: Representation theory defines a Fourier transform on groups. Finite commutative groups correspond to the classical discrete Fourier transform. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Representation_theory_of_finite_groups https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fourier_transform_on_finite_groups

title: Hairy Ball
content: The hairy ball theorem states that in odd dimension d, vector fields on the tangent plane of a (d-1)-sphere necessarily contain a singular point (where it vanishes). https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hairy_ball_theorem

title: Push Fwd
content: Pullback of functions and pushforward of measures are dual one with each other. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pullback https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pushforward_measure

title: Haar Transform
content: Haar transform: only + and - yet surprisingly powerful. The first example of wavelet transform. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Haar_wavelet

title: Minkowski
content: Minkowski inequality states that the l^p norm is a norm. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Minkowski_inequality

title: Heat Wave Schro
content: Heat, Wave and Schrodinger equations are fundamental linear partial differential equations of physics. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heat_equation https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wave_equation https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Schr%C3%B6dinger_equation

title: Hopfield
content: Hopfield networks are recurrent networks minimizing an Ising-type energy parameterized by its weights. Learning weights means encoding patterns of +1/-1 as local minimizers. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hopfield_network

title: Approx Quantiz
content: Approximation vs quantization: two ways to compress. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quantization https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Function_approximation

title: Holder Ineq
content: Holder inequality generalizes Cauchy-Schwarz to arbitrary exponents. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/H%C3%B6lder%27s_inequality

title: Lloyd Surface
content: Lloyd algorithm can be applied on a surface using the geodesic Voronoi diagram. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lloyd%27s_algorithm http://nbviewer.jupyter.org/github/gpeyre/numerical-tours/blob/master/matlab/fastmarching_4_mesh.ipynb

title: Fluid Incompress
content: Navier Stokes equation describes the motion of an incompressible viscous fluid. It is non-linear because the flow is advected by itself. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navier%E2%80%93Stokes_equations http://nbviewer.jupyter.org/github/gpeyre/numerical-tours/blob/master/python/graphics_5_fluids.ipynb

title: Curve Approx
content: Curve approximation using Fourier series corresponds to drawing the curve using entangled ellipses. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fourier_series

title: Soft Max
content: Differentiable max & argmax operators are defined through concave maximization on the simplex. Soft and sparse max are particular cases. https://arxiv.org/abs/1602.02068 https://arxiv.org/abs/1705.07704 https://arxiv.org/abs/1802.03676 https://arxiv.org/abs/1802.04223

title: Hypercube
content: The hypercube (tesseract in dimension 4) is the d-dimensional cube. It can be visualized by projection on a rotating 3-D space. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tesseract https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hypercube

title: Max Gaussians
content: The max of n independent Gaussians concentrates around sqrt(2log(n)). The max central limit theorem allows to quantify this. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fisher%E2%80%93Tippett%E2%80%93Gnedenko_theorem

title: Tv Denoise
content: Total variation denoising can be solved by doing a projected gradient descent on the dual problem. The same idea applies to SVM with ridge regularization. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Total_variation_denoising

title: Woodbury Formula
content: Woodbury formula allows one to compute in two different ways the solution of Ridge regression. It allows one to even use infinite-dimensional feature spaces (p=inf) via kernelization. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Woodbury_matrix_identity https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tikhonov_regularization

title: Edge Flip
content: Triangulated graphs are maximal planar graphs, i.e., for which one cannot add an extra edge (without breaking planarity). The set of triangulated graphs is itself a connected graph when one navigates using "edge flips." https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flip_graph https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flip_graph

title: Weiszfeld Algo
content: Weiszfeld's algorithm is an iterative least square method to compute medians (p=1) and, in general, sums of distance to some power p. Using p<2 makes the solution robust to outliers.

title: Wave Schro
content: Space-invariant PDEs can be solved in closed form (without time integration) using the Fourier transform. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Partial_differential_equation

title: Harm Spher
content: The spherical Laplacian defines a set of orthogonal eigenspaces spanned by spherical harmonics. Display here is a random evolution in each space. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spherical_harmonics

title: Displ Interp
content: Displacement Interpolation, introduced by R McCann, is the optimal transport geodesic between 2 point clouds, more generally btw measures. Interpreting the space of measures as a manifold has countless implications and applications in physics, chemistry, signal processing, ML...

title: Mobius Transf
content: Mobius transforms are the bijective conformal maps from the Riemann sphere (complex numbers with a point at infinity) to itself. They are rational functions, form a group under composition, and have, in general, two fixed points (in black). https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/M%C3%B6bius_transformation

title: Fisher Rao
content: The Fisher-Rao distance is the geodesic distance associated with smooth divergences (e.g., Kulback-Leibler). Without constraint, it is the Hellinger distance. On the manifold of Gaussians, it is a negatively curved space. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fisher_information_metric

title: Lambert Phong
content: Lambert and Phong illumination models are the most well-known empirical models of surface reflectance. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gouraud_shading https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phong_reflection_model https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lambertian_reflectance

title: Schrod Pbm
content: The Shrodinger problem defines a dynamic interpolation between two distributions using Brownian bridges. The 0 temperature limit is Optimal Transport. https://hal.archives-ouvertes.fr/hal-00849930/document

title: Legendre Lp
content: The Legendre-Fenchel transform extends the Legendre transform to arbitrary dimensions. |x|^2/2 is the only fixed point of the transform. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Legendre_transformation

title: Proximal Map
content: The proximal map projects on a level set. For l^p norms, it is a thresholding operator shrinking toward 0. It induces sparsity for p smaller than 1. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Proximal_operator

title: Simplicial Cpx
content: Simplicial complexes are combinatorial objects generalizing triangulations. They are central to (computational) homology and topological data analysis. Two examples for embedded points are alpha and Chech complexes. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Simplicial_complex

title: Inverse Kin
content: Numerical inverse kinematics solves an ill-posed inverse problem (non-unique solution) by gradient descent, thereby leveraging an "implicit bias" (favoring minimal displacements). It is at the heart of robotics and CG animation. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inverse_kinematics

title: Aniso Diffusion
content: Anisotropic diffusion uses space-varyingg conductivity to slow down diffusion near edges, resulting in non-isotropic diffusion behavior. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anisotropic_diffusion

title: Toland Duality
content: Toland's duality for non-convex optimization (difference of convex functions) is surprisingly useful when the dual happens to be convex. A nice paper by Guillaume Carlier explores this concept. https://www.ceremade.dauphine.fr/~carlier/toland.pdf

title: Kaczmarz Algo
content: Kaczmarz's algorithm corresponds to the iterative projection on the hyper-space defined by the columns. Here, the worst possible ordering of the constraints is displayed. Using random selection helps a lot. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kaczmarz_method

title: Backprop
content: Back-propagation for feed-forward architecture is a special case of reverse-mode automatic differentiation. It computes the gradient of a loss function with a cost comparable to the computation of the loss function itself. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Backpropagation

title: Steiner Trees
content: The Euclidean Steiner tree looks for the shortest irrigation tree of nodes. At most p-2 extra (Steiner) points are needed, and they have a degree of 3 with an angle of 120 deg. Unlike the minimum spanning tree problem (without Steiner points), no efficient algorithm exists. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steiner_tree...

title: Nash
content: Classic reference: J. Nash, The Imbedding Problem for Riemannian Manifolds, 1956, C^1 n-dimensional manifolds can be isometrically embedded in dimension 2n, defining "fractal" like surfaces. This contrasts with smooth manifolds (which requires n(n+2)/2 dimensions).

title: Boosting
content: Boosting methods compute a strong classifier as a weighted sum of weak classifiers. The optimization is performed by a greedy coordinate minimization. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boosting_(machine_learning)

title: Ista
content: Classic reference: Daubechies, M. Defrise, C. De Mol, An iterative thresholding algorithm for linear inverse problems with a sparsity constraint, 2004. The celebrated Iterative Soft Thresholding algorithm to solve the LASSO is a special case of the Forward-Backward algorithm. http://nbviewer.jupyter.org/github/gpeyr...

title: Jl Lemma
content: The Johnson-Lindenstrauss lemma shows that one can project linearly m points in dimension log(m)/epsilon^2 with distortion epsilon. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johnson%E2%80%93Lindenstrauss_lemma

title: Zeta Func
content: Classic reference: Bernhard Riemann, Ueber die Anzahl der Primzahlen unter einer gegebenen Grosse, 1859. Riemann hypothesis states that the only non-trivial zeros of the zeta function are on the line Re(s)=1/2. One of the the most celebrated mathematical conjecture. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Riemann_zeta_function

title: Kernel Svm
content: Support vector machines (SVM) can be used to define curved decision boundaries using the kernel trick. It implicitly makes use of an infinite dimensional feature lifting. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kernel_method

title: Delaunay
content: Classic reference: B. Delaunay, Sur la sphere vide, 1934. Introduces the concept of Delaunay triangulation, which is the dual of the Voronoi diagram. The most fundamental tool of computational geometry. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Delaunay_triangulation https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Voronoi_diagram https://en.wiki...

title: Voronoi Pruning
content: Pruning the Voronoi diagram of a set of points is way to estimate the medial axis of a smooth curve. Used in many shape reconstruction methods. http://web.cs.ucdavis.edu/~amenta/pubs/crust.pdf http://web.cse.ohio-state.edu/~dey.8/paper/medial.pdf

title: Runge
content: Classic reference: Carl Runge, Über empirische Funktionen und die Interpolation zwischen äquidistanten Ordinaten, 1901. Oscillations are introduced by polynomial interpolation at equi-spaced grid points. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Runge%27s_phenomenon

title: Psd Matrices
content: Positive semi-definite matrices come in many flavors! https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Definite_symmetric_matrix

title: Aliasing
content: Classic reference: Franklin Crow, The aliasing problem in computer-generated shaded images, 1977. Laid the foundations of anti-aliasing (i.e. pre-filtering) technics (classical in analog signal acquisition) for computer generated images. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spatial_anti-aliasing

title: Floyd Warshall
content: Floyd-Warshall algorithm computes all pairs shortest distances. Related to iterative powering of the adjacency matrix for the (min, +) algebra from Tropical geometry. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Floyd%E2%80%93Warshall_algorithm https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Min-plus_matrix_multiplication https://en.wikipedia.org/w...

title: A Trou
content: Classic reference: M Holschneider, R Kronland-Martinet, J Morlet, P Tchamitchian, A Real-Time Algorithm for Signal Analysis with the Help of the Wavelet Transform, 1990. The "a trou" algorithm computes convolution with large filters as a product of dilated filters. Useful to replace "strided" (i.e. subsampled) neura...

title: Qda
content: Quadratic discriminant analysis is a supervised classification method computing a maximum likelihood for Gaussian model. Linear discriminant analysis is the special case where the covariances are equal, and corresponds to the computation of Voronoi cells. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Linear_discriminant_analysis

title: Partial Smoothness
content: Oldies but goodies: A.S. Lewis. Active sets, nonsmoothness, and sensitivity, 2002. Partial smoothness is the correct notion of "piecewise smooth functions" in optimization. Useful to study active set methods and relate optimization to differential geometry. https://hal.archives-ouvertes.fr/hal-00987293

title: Pseudo Spectrum
content: The pseudo-spectrum defines sets that encapsulate the eigenvalues. Their shape gives information about how ill-conditioned the spectrum is. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pseudospectrum

title: Svm
content: Classic reference: V.N. Vapnik, A.J. Chervonenkis, On the uniform convergence of relative frequencies of events to their probabilities. Defines the notion of VC dimension to ensure classification bounds of statistical learning methods, and introduces support-vector machines. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/VC_dimension

title: Filtering
content: Iterating filters with small supports is equivalent to using a filter with an increasing size. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Convolution

title: Minkowski
content: Classic reference: Hermann Minkowski, Geometrie der Zahlen, 1896. The Brunn-Minkowski inequality is one of the fundamental inequalities in convex geometry, which generalizes the isoperimetric inequality. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brunn%E2%80%93Minkowski_theorem https://terrytao.wordpress.com/tag/brunn-minkowski-...

title: Invariant Measure
content: Invariant measures are fundamental for the study of dynamical systems. Replace the study of non-linear maps by the calculus of a linear eigenvector (fixed point of the push-forward operator). https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Invariant_measure

title: Bregman
content: Classic reference: Bregman, The relaxation method of finding the common points of convex sets, 1967. Bregman divergences are convex distance-like functionals which are locally Euclidean. Many algorithm generalizes to Bregman geometries. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bregman_divergence

title: Conformal
content: A map is conformal (angle preserving) if and only if it is holomorphic with a non-vanishing derivative. The map wraps around singular points where the derivative vanishes. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conformal_map https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Holomorphic_function

title: Hopfield
content: Classic reference: J. Hopfield, Neural networks and physical systems with emergent collective computational abilities, 1982. Hopfield networks are recurrent networks minimizing an Ising-type energy parameterized by its weights. Learning weights means encoding patterns of +1/-1 as local minimizers. https://en.wikiped...

title: Good Triangulation
content: A good triangulation to solve stably elliptic PDEs should contains isotropic triangles. Meshing complicated domain is an art requiring grading triangle sizes. https://people.eecs.berkeley.edu/~jrs/papers/elemtalk.pdf

title: Schrod Eq
content: Classic reference: E. Schrodinger, An Undulatory Theory of the Mechanics of Atoms and Molecules, 1926. Introduces the now-called Schrodinger equation governing the evolution of the wave function of quantum particles. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Schr%C3%B6dinger_equation

title: Fiedler Vec
content: The Fiedler vector of a graph is the second eigenvector of the Laplacian. It is the lowest "Fourier" mode and is useful to order the nodes (clustering, dimensionality reduction, etc). https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Algebraic_connectivity

title: Turbo Codes
content: Classic reference: C. Berrou, A. Glavieux, P. Thitimajshima, Near Shannon Limit Error-correcting Coding and Decoding: Turbo-codes, 1993. Turbo codes were invented by Claude Berrou. It revolutionized convolutional error correcting codes. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Turbo_code

title: Poly Interp
content: Oscillations are introduced by polynomial interpolation at equi-spaced grid points. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Runge%27s_phenomenon https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chebyshev_nodes

title: Weierstrass Func
content: Oldie but goldie. Karl Weierstrass, Uber continuirliche Functionen eines reellen Arguments, die fur keinen Werth des letzeren einen bestimmten Differentialquotienten besitzen, 1895. First example of a nowhere differentiable continuous function. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Weierstrass_function

title: Pca
content: Principal component analysis projects the data on the leading eigenvectors of the covariance matrix. Optimal linear dimensionality reduction in a least square sense. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Principal_component_analysis http://nbviewer.ipython.org/github/gpeyre/numerical-tours/blob/master/python/ml_1_pca_nn.ipynb

title: Lll
content: Classic reference: A. Lenstra; H. Lenstra, L. Lovasz, Factoring polynomials with rational coefficients, 1982. The LLL algorithm approximately solves the shortest vector problem in a lattice (which is simple in low dimension). https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lenstra%E2%80%93Lenstra%E2%80%93Lov%C3%A1sz_lattice_basis_red...

title: Density Estimation
content: Density estimation can be performed using kernels or nearest-neighbors. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Density_estimation

title: Chambolle Tv
content: Classic reference: A. Chambolle, An algorithm for total variation minimization and applications, 2004. Total variation denoising can be solved by doing a projected gradient descent on the dual problem. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Total_variation_denoising

title: Smoothing Splines
content: Smoothing splines define regularized least square whose solutions are sums of kernel functions (special case of reproducing Hilbert space). Linear interpolation and cubic splines are special cases. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smoothing_spline

title: Cont Wavelets
content: Classic reference: J. Morlet and A. Grossmann, Decomposition of Hardy functions into square integrable wavelets of constant shape, 1984. Studies the continuous wavelet transform, introduced by Morlet in geophysics. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Morlet_wavelet

title: Numerical Range
content: The numerical range of a matrix is the range of the Rayleigh quotient. It is a convex set enclosing the eigenvalues. This enclosing is tight for maximally "stable" (normal) matrices. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Numerical_range

title: Shepp Logan
content: Classic reference: L. A. Shepp. and B. F. Logan The Fourier reconstruction of a head section, 1974. Introduces the filtered back-projection, which is the basic method to invert of the Radon transform and is used for reconstructing images in tomographic imaging. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shepp%E2%80%93Logan_phantom

title: Ising
content: The Ising model is one of the most celebrated model from statistical physics exhibiting a phase transition at a critical temperature in dimension 2 and higher. Models variety of phenomena from ferromagnet to neural networks. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Square_lattice_Ising_model

title: Shapiro Ineq
content: Classic reference: V. G. Drinfeld, A cyclic inequality, 1971. For n=2k<=12 and n=2k+1<=23, the optimal value of cyclic sums is n/2 (Shapiro's inequality). This paper proved that asymptotically, these sums gets smaller than n/2 by 1%. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shapiro_inequality

title: Ortho Matrices
content: Orthogonal matrices come with lots of flavours! https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orthogonal_matrix

title: Bcr Algo
content: Classic reference: G. Beylkin, R. Coifman, V. Rokhlin, Fast wavelet transforms and numerical algorithms, 1991. Linear time wavelet-based algorithm to apply smooth integral operators. http://nbviewer.jupyter.org/github/gpeyre/numerical-tours/blob/master/matlab/pde_4_wavelet_compression.ipynb

title: Minkowski Ineq
content: If p<1, then it is the l^p functional to the power p which satisfies the triangular inequality (Minkowski inequality).

title: Mlp Approx
content: Classic reference: V. Maiorov and A. Pinkus, Lower bounds for approximation by MLP neural network, 1999. Use Kolmogorov-Arnold superposition to construct a smooth activation function so that 2 hidden layer MLP with a fixed number of neurons are universal. Hint: sigma is not a relu! https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kolm...

title: Assignement Pbm
content: The assignment problem is a combinatorial optimization problem which can be solved in log(n) n^3 operations. It is a special case of Optimal Transport. For the Euclidean distance cost, trajectories do not cross. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Assignment_problem

title: Max Clt
content: Classic reference: R. Fisher and L. Tippett, Limiting forms of the frequency distribution of the largest and smallest member of a sample, 1928. Central limit theorem for the maximum of variables. Limit distribution can only be either Frechet, Gumbel or Weibull. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fisher%E2%80%93Tippett%E2...

title: Semi Algebraic
content: Tarski-Seidenberg theorem in action: the set of polynomials having a real root is semi-algebraic. Coste provides the block diagram for degree 4 in his notes! http://gcomte.perso.math.cnrs.fr/M2/CosteIntroToSemialGeo.pdf

title: Sparse Coding
content: Classic reference: B. Olshausen, D. Field, Emergence of simple-cell receptive field properties by learning a sparse code for natural images, 1996. Showed that dictionary learning on natural image produces wavelet-like atoms. https://www.nature.com/articles/381607a0

title: Sgd
content: Stochastic gradient descent is the workhorse of many large scale machine learning methods. Allows one to minimize functions written as expectations. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stochastic_gradient_descent https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stochastic_approximation

title: Boosting
content: Classic reference: Yoav Freund et Robert Schapire, A decision-theoretic generalization of on-line learning and an application to boosting, 1997. Introduces AdaBoost, the most popular boosting method, to define a strong classifier from weak ones. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AdaBoost

title: Convolution
content: Convolutions are the translation invariant linear operators (filtering). https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Convolution

title: Sunflower
content: Classic reference: H. Vogel, A better way to construct the sunflower head, 1979. Describe spiraling patterns in nature, foundational paper in mathematical phyllotaxis. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phyllotaxis

title: Cauchy Binnet
content: Cauchy-Binet formula generalizes the determinant of a product of square matrices to the general rectangular case. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cauchy%E2%80%93Binet_formula

title: Joukowski
content: Classic reference: Joukowsky, N.E., Uber die Konturen der Tragflachen der Drachenflieger, 1910. The Joukowsky conformal map solves airfoil design in the pre-computer era. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joukowsky_transform

title: Kernel Pca
content: Kernel PCA defines a non-linear dimensionality reduction by applying a linear principal component analysis over a lifted feature space. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kernel_principal_component_analysis

title: Ellastic Net
content: Oldies but goodies: Zou, Hastie, Regularization and variable selection via the elastic net, 2005. Interpolates between the Lasso (l1) and Ridge regression (l2). The regularization path of Lasso is polygonal. The one of elastic net is piecewise smooth. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elastic_net_regularization

title: Graphical Lasso
content: Conditional independence of entries of Gaussian vectors defines a graph associated to the inverse of the covariance (precision matrix). Graphical Lasso estimates a sparse graph by l^1 penalizing the maximum likelihood estimator. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Graphical_lasso

title: Jpeg2K
content: Classic reference: David Taubman, High performance scalable image compression with EBCOT, 2000. JPEG2000 performs an advanced arithmetic coding of Wavelets coefficients of the image. Coefficients are quantized and coded bit by bit to provide a progressive coding. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/JPEG_2000

title: Moving Least Squares
content: Moving least square is a mesh-free interpolation method which performs a localized weighted least square with singular weights. The case of constant polynomial is Shepard's method. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moving_least_squares

title: Wirtinger
content: Classic reference: Wilhelm Wirtinger, Zur formalen Theorie der Funktionen von mehr komplexen Veränderlichen, 1926. Wirtinger derivatives treat complex valued functions of complex variables as if they were real functions. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wirtinger_derivatives

title: Kernel Ridge
content: Kernel ridge regression approximates a function using a sum of kernel functions. The kernel must be symmetric positive semi-definite, for instance Gaussian or Laplacian. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kernel_method

title: Nmf
content: Classic reference: D. Lee et S. Seung, Learning the parts of objects by non-negative matrix factorization, Nature (1999). Lee and Seung proposed the most popular matrix factorization algorithm, which operates by multiplicative updates. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Non-negative_matrix_factorization

title: Hermite
content: Hermite functions form an ortho-basis of the continuous Fourier transform. Coming up with their discrete counterpart (discrete eigenvectors of the FFT) is surprisingly hard and apparently still mostly an open problem. https://arxiv.org/pdf/1501.07646.pdf

title: Ica
content: Classic reference: Pierre Comon, Independent component analysis, a new concept? , 1994. Gives a rigorous definition of the ICA as an optimization problem, leveraging non-Gaussianity and independence of the sources. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Independent_component_analysis

title: Mirror Descent
content: For small step sizes, mirror descent is equivalent to a gradient descent on a Hessian manifold. https://blogs.princeton.edu/imabandit/2013/04/16/orf523-mirror-descent-part-iii/

title: Matern
content: Classic reference: B. Matern, Spatial Variation, 1960. The Matern kernel interpolates between Laplacian and Gaussian. The most popular kernels in ML, allows to represents functions with a given smoothness nu (number of derivative) for regression and classification using RKHS. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mat%C3%A9r...

title: Roots Poles
content: Vizualizing zeros and poles of rational functions over the complex plane. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zeros_and_poles https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pole%E2%80%93zero_plot

title: Catmull
content: Classic reference: Edwin Catmull, A hidden-surface algorithm with anti-aliasing, 1974. This PhD thesis laid the foundation of rending, in particular the Z-buffer and anti-aliasing. https://syncedreview.com/2020/04/25/turing-award-a-closer-look-into-edwin-catmulls-phd-thesis/

title: Zeta
content: Riemann hypothesis states that the only non-trivial zeros of the zeta functions are on the line Re(s)=1/2. One of the the most celebrated mathematical conjecture. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Riemann_zeta_function

title: Bilateral Filter
content: Classic reference: C. Tomasi and R. Manduchi, "Bilateral Filtering for Gray and Color Images", Proceedings of the 1998. The basic method for edge preserving filtering.

title: Heat Poly
content: The heat equation on polynomials (for the differential on the complex plane) generates complex dynamics on the roots. https://terrytao.wordpress.com/2017/10/17/heat-flow-and-zeroes-of-polynomials/

title: Hungarian
content: Classic reference: H. Kuhn, The Hungarian Method for the assignment problem, 1955. The most celebrated algorithm to solve efficiently (almost cubic time) the assignment problem. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hungarian_algorithm

title: Walsh Haar
content: Only + and - operations: Walsh-Rademacher-Hadamard vs Haar transforms. Dense vs sparse (for piecewise constant inputs). https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hadamard_transform https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Haar_wavelet

title: Dublin
content: Dubins paths are shortest path for cars which can only move forward. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dubins_path

title: Kmeans
content: Classic reference: J. B. MacQueen, Some Methods for classification and Analysis of Multivariate Observations, 1967. Introduces the k-means algorithm, which is a discrete version of Lloyd algorithm for optimal quantization. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/K-means_clustering

title: Chromatic Number
content: Computing the chromatic number of a graph is NP hard. It is at most 4 for planar graphs. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Four_color_theorem

title: Dijkstra Algo
content: Classic reference: E. W. Dijkstra, A note on two problems in connexion with graphs, 1959. Dijkstra's algorithm computes the geodesic distance on a graph in O(n log(n)) operations using a front propagation algorithm. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dijkstra%27s_algorithm

title: Chebyshev Poly
content: Zeros of Chebyshev defines grids point optimal for the uniform convergence of polynomial interpolation. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chebyshev_polynomials

title: Von Neumann
content: Classic reference: J. von Neumann, On rings of operators, 1949. Computes a point in the intersection of two convex sets via alternating projections. Works well in practice also for non-convex sets. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Projections_onto_convex_sets https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dykstra%27s_projection_algorithm

title: Lagrange Hermite
content: Lagrange and Hermite interpolations can be solved in closed form using Lagrange polynomials. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagrange_polynomial https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hermite_interpolation https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Polynomial_interpolation

title: Johnson Lindenstrauss
content: Classic reference: W. B. Johnson and J. Lindenstrauss, Extensions of Lipschitz maps into a Hilbert space, 1984. Shows that one can project linearly m points in dimension log(m)/epsilon^2 with distortion epsilon. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johnson%E2%80%93Lindenstrauss_lemma

title: Precision Matrix
content: Inverse of Laplacian matrix can be used to define covariance kernels with positive pairwise correlations between nodes. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laplacian_matrix

title: Alex Net
content: Classic reference: A Krizhevsky, I Sutskever, G Hinton, Imagenet classification with deep convolutional neural networks, 2012. Sparkle the explosion of deep learning by significantly improving the sate of the art for image classification. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AlexNet

title: Prime Numbers
content: The prime number theorem is the most celebrated theorem of number theory. Contrary to what numerics suggest, pi(n) is not always smaller than the logarithm integral! https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prime-counting_function

title: Grad Flows
content: Classic reference: Luigi Ambrosio, Nicola Gigli, Giuseppe Savare, Gradient Flows In Metric Spaces and in the Space of Probability Measures, 2005. Formalize the notion of descent methods on non-Euclidean domains without using a gradient. http://www.springer.com/la/book/9783764387211

title: Qr Algo
content: The QR algorithm repeatedly applies the QR decomposition to generate a sequence of orthogonal semblable matrices converging to a triangular one. This gem from matrix analysis is the workhorse of dense eigen-solvers. Its convergence remains an open problem in full generality. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/QR_algorithm

title: Auctions
content: Classic reference: D. Bertsekas. A distributed algorithm for the assignment problem, 1979. A very elegant algorithm to solve efficiently (almost cubic time) the assignment problem. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Auction_algorithm

title: Mean Field
content: A mean field evolution is the large number limit of particles systems. The simplest case is gradient descent, which corresponds to an advection equation in the limit. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Advection https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mean_field_theory

title: Levin Np
content: Classic reference: Leonid Levin, Universal search problems, 1973. Introduced with Cook the notion of NP-completeness and proved that SAT is NP-complete. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cook%E2%80%93Levin_theorem

title: Gen Means
content: Generalized means interpolate between the min, the geometric mean, the arithmetic mean and the max. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generalized_mean

title: Tarski
content: Classic reference: A. Tarski, A decision method for elementary algebra and geometry, 1951. Semi-algebraicity is stable by projection. The most fundamental result in semi-algebraic geometry. Equivalent to the elimination of the existential quantifier. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tarski%E2%80%93Seidenberg_theorem

title: Nonlin Diffusion
content: Nonlinearity matters. Linear diffusion (heat) has non-compactly supported solutions. Non-linear diffusion (porous medium) drives dynamics with compactly supported solutions. The porous medium is the simplest case, studied in details by Otto. https://www.mis.mpg.de/preprints/1999/preprint1999_8.pdf

title: Reeds Shepp
content: Classic reference: Reeds, J.A. and L.A. Shepp, Optimal paths for a car that goes both forwards and backwards, 1990. Generalize Dubins paths for cars that can move both forward and backward. https://programmersought.com/article/1869834830/

title: Arith Geom
content: Iterating arithmetic and geometric means quickly (quadratically) converges to the so-called arithmetic geometric mean. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arithmetic%E2%80%93geometric_mean

title: Cook Np
content: Classic reference: Stephen Cook, The Complexity of Theorem Proving Procedures, 1971. Introduced with Levin the notion of NP-completeness and proved that SAT is NP-complete. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cook%E2%80%93Levin_theorem

title: Spectrogram
content: The spectrogram (also known as short time Fourier transform) reveals the geometry of sounds. Evolving harmonics of a bird's singing become smooth curves. Sounds are intrinsically (at least) 2-D (time-frequency). https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spectrogram https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Short-time_Fourier_transform

title: Geman Geman
content: Classic reference: Geman, S.; Geman, D. Stochastic Relaxation, Gibbs Distributions, and the Bayesian Restoration of Images, 1984. Introduces the Gibbs sampler. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gibbs_sampling

title: Gershgorin Disk
content: Gershgorin circle theorem locates the eigenvalues of a matrix in the union of disks centered at the diagonal entries. Implies invertibility of diagonally dominant matrices. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gershgorin_circle_theorem

title: Spectral Graph
content: Classic reference: F. Chung, Spectral Graph Theory. Everything you want to know about the Laplacian of a graph! http://www.math.ucsd.edu/~fan/research/revised.html

title: Means Evol
content: The geometric, arithmetic, and arithmetic-geometric means can be extended to complex numbers. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arithmetic%E2%80%93geometric_mean

title: Tukey Filter
content: Classic reference: John Tukey, Exploratory data analysis, 1977. Introduced robust statistics methods and in particular median filtering. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Exploratory_data_analysis

title: Dubin Paths
content: Dubins' paths (i.e. shortest path for a car which cannot go backwards) define a distance that depends on the starting/ending direction. It is in general not continuous. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dubins_path

title: Gumbel
content: Classic reference: B. Gnedenko, Sur la distribution limite du terme maximum d'une serie aleatoire, 1943. The Fisher-Tippett-Gnedenko theorem gives the distribution of the limit of the maximum of a large number of random variables. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fisher%E2%80%93Tippett%E2%80%93Gnedenko_theorem

title: Lda
content: Linear discriminant analysis is a maximum likelihood classification method for Gaussian model with the same covariance for all the classes. It corresponds to the computation of Voronoi cells. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Linear_discriminant_analysis

title: Barron
content: Classic reference: A. Barron, Universal Approximation Bounds for Superpositions of a Sigmoidal Function, 1993. Proves that 1 hidden layer perceptrons break the curse of dimensionality to approximate a class of smooth functions. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Universal_approximation_theorem https://en.wikipedia.org/wi...

title: A Trou
content: "à trou" algorithm computes convolution with a large filter as a product of dilated filters. Useful to replace "strided" (subsampled) neural networks by translation-invariant networks. Useful to compute translation-invariant wavelet transforms. Relies on a nice commutation formula!

title: Gsm
content: Classic reference: M. Wainwright, E. Simoncelli, Scale Mixtures of Gaussians and the Statistics of Natural Images, 1999. Popularized GSM to model heavy-tailed data distributions. https://papers.nips.cc/paper/1750-scale-mixtures-of-gaussians-and-the-statistics-of-natural-images.pdf

title: Cubic Curve
content: Through nine points in generic position passes a single cubic curve. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cubic_plane_curve

title: Nadaraya Watson
content: Classic reference: E. A. Nadaraya, On Estimating Regression, 1964. Nadaraya-Watson regression performs a localized barycentric average of the input values. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kernel_regression

title: 3D Heat
content: The heat equation in 3D smoothes all the level sets of a function. Generates melting surfaces! https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heat_equation

title: Stein Lemma
content: Classic reference: C. Stein, A bound for the error in the normal approximation to the distribution of a sum of dependent random variables, 1972. Uses Stein's lemma to derive bounds for convergence rates in the central limit theorem. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stein%27s_lemma https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stein%27...

title: Optimal Assignment
content: The assignment problem is relaxed to Optimal Transport by considering arbitrary probability distributions (a, b) on the points. The "matching" is only twice less sparse. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Optimal_matching

title: Kernel Methods
content: Classic reference: Aizerman, Braverman, Rozoner, Theoretical foundations of the potential function method in pattern recognition learning, 1964. Early appearance of kernel methods for learning. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kernel_perceptron

title: Kernel Pca
content: Classic reference: B Schölkopf, A Smola, K-R Müller, Nonlinear Component Analysis as a Kernel Eigenvalue Problem, 1998. Kernel PCA defines a non-linear dimensionality reduction by applying a linear principal component analysis over a lifted feature space. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kernel_principal_component_anal...

title: Maxent
content: Many parametric probability distribution families can be written as maximum entropy distributions. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maximum_entropy_probability_distribution

title: Cotan Laplacian
content: Classic reference: G. Dziuk, Finite elements for the Beltrami operator on arbitrary surfaces, 1988. Rigorous analysis of the cotan weights Laplacian (P1 finite elements on triangulations).

title: Relu Networks
content: A ReLu network computes a piecewise linear approximation of a target function. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rectifier_(neural_networks)

title: Brockett Flow
content: Classic reference: R. Brockett, Dynamical systems that sort lists, diagonalize matrices, and solve linear programming problems, 1991. Brockett's flow progressively diagonalizes a symmetric matrix. http://hrl.harvard.edu/publications/brockett88dynamical.pdf

title: Fourier Noncom
content: Fourier transform on groups turns convolution into multiplication. For non-commutative groups, it is matrix-matrix multiplication though … https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fourier_transform_on_finite_groups https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Convolution_theorem

title: Lojasiewicz
content: Classic reference: S. Lojasiewicz: Une propriete topologique des sous-ensembles analytiques reels, 1962. Kurdyka-Łojasiewicz property is fundamental to study convergence of descent optimization methods. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/%C5%81ojasiewicz_inequality

title: Toeplitz Conjecture
content: Toeplitz' conjecture asks whether every planar simple closed curve contains the vertices of a square. It is true for convex or smooth curves. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inscribed_square_problem

title: Mean Curv
content: Classic reference: B Merriman, J Bence, S Osher, Diffusion generated motion by mean curvature, 1992. Iteration of filtering and thresholding implements the mean-curvature flow. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mean_curvature_flow

title: Mle
content: MLE estimates the parameters of a distribution by maximizing a likelihood. In the large number of samples limit, it minimizes the relative entropy between the data and the parametric distribution. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maximum_likelihood_estimation
