Propose to use non-convex methods to solve large-scale convex problems, a very influential idea. http://www.optimization-online.org/DB_FILE/2001/03/296.pdf

title: Bilateral Filter
content: The bilateral filter is a non-linear edge-preserving filter where weights operate on both space and range values. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bilateral_filter

title: Karmarkar
content: Classic reference: Narendra Karmarkar, A New Polynomial Time Algorithm for Linear Programming, 1984. First efficient interior point method solving linear programs in polynomial time. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karmarkar%27s_algorithm

title: Sparse Factors
content: Sparse Cholesky factorization is obtained by applying the algorithm after a careful reordering of the rows/columns. The minimum degree heuristic is surprisingly efficient. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Minimum_degree_algorithm

title: Chew Algo
content: Classic reference: Paul Chew, Guaranteed-quality mesh generation for curved surfaces, 1993. With Ruppert's method, the first algorithm for provably good quality meshing of constrained domains. Based on Delaunay refinement. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chew%27s_second_algorithm

title: Moreau Smooth
content: Moreau-Yosida regularization smoothes a function. It is the inf-convolution with a quadratic function. Its gradient is Id - the proximal operator. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Convex_conjugate#Infimal_convolution

title: Coarea
content: Classic reference: Herbert Federer, Curvature measures, 1959. The co-area formula expresses the Total Variation semi-norm as the total perimeters of level sets. Enables the computation of TV for non-smooth functions. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coarea_formula

title: Saddle
content: Saddle points come with lots of flavors. Quadratic saddle are non-degenerate and repulse gradient descent. Higher-order saddle points can attract gradient descent in a lot of directions. http://www.offconvex.org/2016/03/22/saddlepoints/ https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saddle_point

title: Kalman
content: Classic reference: R.E. Kalman, A New Approach to Linear Filtering and Prediction Problems, 1960. Kalman filter defines recursively an estimator of the parameters of a Gaussian dynamical process. Basic method to control navigation systems. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kalman_filter

title: Projections
content: The unreasonable effectiveness of non-smooth optimization: sharp singularities attract solutions of optimization problems (here a projection on a set).

title: John Ellipse
content: Classic reference: Fritz John, Extremum problems with inequalities as subsidiary conditions, 1948. Proves the uniqueness of a maximum enclosed ellipsoid for compact convex sets.

title: Enveloppe
content: The envelope of a set of curves is another curve tangent to all these curves. Caustics are a particular case. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Envelope_(mathematics)

title: Cellular Autom
content: Classic reference: S. Wolfram, Statistical mechanics of cellular automata, 1983. Studies cellular automata and the chaotic behavior of certain rules such as rule 30. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cellular_automaton

title: Minmax
content: Gradient descent/ascent can be inefficient in finding saddle point (Nash equilibrium) for min-max games, because of spiraling behavior. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nash_equilibrium

title: Geodesics Fmm
content: Classic reference: Ron Kimmel, James Sethian, Computing geodesic paths on manifolds, 1998. Extends the fast marching method to work on triangulated surfaces. http://www.pnas.org/content/95/15/8431

title: Phi Diverg
content: Csiszar divergences compare the relative densities of two measures with 1. Does not require any reference measure. Handles arbitrary measures (discrete or continuous). https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/F-divergence

title: Conv Hull
content: Classic reference: David G. Kirkpatrick and Raimund Seidel, The ultimate planar convex hull algorithm? , 1986. The first output-sensitive optimal 2D convex hull algorithm runs in O(n log(h)) for a hull of h points among n. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kirkpatrick%E2%80%93Seidel_algorithm

title: Error Diffusion
content: Error diffusion is the simplest dithering algorithm which quantizes an image to binary values. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Error_diffusion https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Floyd%E2%80%93Steinberg_dithering

title: Isomap
content: Classic reference: J. B. Tenenbaum, V. de Silva, J. C. Langford, A Global Geometric Framework for Nonlinear Dimensionality Reduction, 2000. Isomap is one of the first manifold learning algorithms. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Isomap

title: Lp Balls
content: The l^p functional is convex and hence a norm for p =1. It is sparsity-inducing for p<=1. The l^1 norm is the heart of the lasso, also known as basis pursuit. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lasso_(statistics)

title: Som
content: Classic reference: Teuvo Kohonen, Self-Organized Formation of Topologically Correct Feature Maps, 1982. Self-organizing maps of Kohonen define a map between a 2D space to the data, by minimizing a quantization error and a regularity penalty. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Self-organizing_map

title: Ica
content: Independent component analysis estimates a mixing matrix leveraging the non-Gaussianity and independence of the sources. Solves a matrix factorization problem. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Independent_component_analysis

title: Nash Eq
content: Classic reference: Nash, John, Equilibrium points in n-person games, 1950. Extend min-max saddle points to several players. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nash_equilibrium

title: Ot 1D
content: There exists a single increasing map between two distributions, it is the optimal transport, and it is defined from the cumulative functions. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Histogram_equalization

title: Kernel Svm
content: Classic reference: Corinna Cortes, Vladimir Vapnik, Support-vector networks, 1995. Defines a kernelized version of the support vector machine of Vapnik, Chervonenkis. Very popular for classification. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Support_vector_machine

title: Moreau Polar
content: Moreau's decomposition generalizes orthogonal decomposition from linear spaces to convex cones. https://www.convexoptimization.com/wikimization/index.php/Moreau's_decomposition_theorem https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Convex_cone

title: Penrose
content: Classic reference: R. Penrose, The role of aesthetics in pure and applied mathematical research, 1974. Penrose tilings are aperiodic tilings obtained using typically 2 isosceles triangles with two types of edge labelings (so 4 types of triangles). A way to generate the tiling is by applying iterative edge splitting...

title: Gaussian Products
content: Gaussian functions are stable under pointwise and convolution products. The Fourier transform interleaves these two algebraic structures.

title: Hamming
content: Classic reference: R. Hamming, Error detecting and error correcting codes, 1950. Introduces the first efficient binary error-correcting codes. Can correct any single-bit error, or detect all single-bit and two-bit errors. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hamming(7,4) https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hamming_code

title: Bregman
content: Bregman divergences are convex distance-like functionals that are locally Euclidean. Most algorithms handling Euclidean distances generalize to Bregman divergences. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bregman_divergence

title: Alpha Shape
content: Classic reference: Herbert Edelsbrunner, David Kirkpatrick, Raimund Seidel, On the shape of a set of points in the plane, 1983. Defines alpha-shapes, a multiscale family of simplicial complexes that generalizes convex hull and is useful for topological data analysis and shape reconstruction. https://en.wikipedia.org...

title: Law Max
content: The max of n independent Gaussians concentrates around sqrt(2log(n)). The max central limit theorem allows one to quantify this. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fisher%E2%80%93Tippett%E2%80%93Gnedenko_theorem

title: Lorenz
content: Classic reference: Edward N. Lorenz, Deterministic nonperiodic flow, 1963. Lorenz attractor is the set of limit trajectories for a simplified mathematical model for atmospheric convection. It has a fractal geometry. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lorenz_system

title: Perron Frob
content: Markov chains with positive transitions converge toward the stationary distribution. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Perron%E2%80%93Frobenius_theorem

title: Kanitza
content: Classic reference: Gaetano Kanizsa, Subjective Contours, 1976. Revitalized the study of illusory contours from Gestalt theory and had a profound impact on computer and biological vision. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Illusory_contours

title: Kalman
content: Kalman filter defines recursively an estimator of the parameters of a Gaussian dynamical process. The basic method to control navigation systems. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kalman_filter

title: Poisson Edit
content: Classic reference: Patrick Perez, Michel Gangnet, Andrew Blake, Poisson Image Editing, 2003. A surprisingly simple method for seamless copy/pasting. https://www.ipol.im/pub/art/2016/163/

title: Daubechies
content: Compactly supported orthogonal wavelets are defined using filter banks. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daubechies_wavelet https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ingrid_Daubechies

title: Shape Drum
content: Classic reference: Mark Kac, Can you hear the shape of a drum? 1966. Non-isometric shapes can have the same Laplacian eigenvalues (spectrum). Displaying here some Laplacian eigenvectors. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hearing_the_shape_of_a_drum

title: Texture Synth
content: Photo-realistic texture synthesis methods perform pixels, patches or more complicated features recopy from the input to the output. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Texture_synthesis

title: Knn
content: Classic reference: Evelyn Fix, Joseph Hodges, Discriminatory analysis, nonparametric discrimination: Consistency properties, 1951. Introduces k-nearest neighbors, which is the baseline non-parametric regression and classification method. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/K-nearest_neighbors_algorithm

title: Mccann
content: Displacement interpolation also known as Optimal Transport: discrete vs continuous. https://hal.archives-ouvertes.fr/hal-00763270

title: Mean Val Interp
content: Classic reference: Michael S. Floater, Mean value coordinates, 2003. The first construction of smooth positive barycentric coordinates for general polygons. Used for interpolation of warpings.

title: Point Process
content: The Poisson point process has a flat power spectrum while the Poisson disk exhibits a desirable "blue noise" spectrum. Matches the arrangement of photoreceptors in the retina. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Supersampling#Poisson_disc https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Point_process https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Halftone

title: Hellinger
content: Classic reference: E. Hellinger, Neue Begrundung der Theorie quadratischer Formen von unendlichvielen Veränderlichen, 1909. Introduces the (now called) Hellinger distance, arguably with the total variation norm the most widely used distance between probability distributions. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hellinger_d...

title: Dft
content: The discrete Fourier basis is a sampling of the continuous Fourier basis. They are both orthogonal. This is (almost) magic! https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Discrete_Fourier_transform

title: Rbf
content: Classic reference: Rolland L. Hardy, Multiquadric equations of topography and other irregular surfaces, 1971. Introduces radial basis functions interpolation. In some cases (e.g. Gaussian and polyharmonic), corresponds to regression in a reproducing Hilbert space. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Radial_basis_function

title: Rosenbrok
content: The Rosenbrock function is the most famous test function for optimization algorithms. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rosenbrock_function

title: Corner Detect
content: Classic reference: Chris Harris, Mike Stephens, A combined corner and edge detector, 1988. The most frequently used corner detector, based on the eigenvalues of the structure tensor. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harris_Corner_Detector

title: Proj Fw
content: Projected gradient and Frank-Wolfe are the cornerstones of constrained optimization. PG typically evolves on the boundary while FW operates as an interior point method. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Frank%E2%80%93Wolfe_algorithm

title: Sinkhorn
content: Classic reference: Richard Sinkhorn, A relationship between arbitrary positive matrices and doubly stochastic matrices, 1964. The first proof of the convergence of the diagonal scaling algorithm (also known as IPFP, RAS, etc) toward a uniquely defined bistochastic matrix. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sinkhorn%27s_t...

title: Advection
content: Gradient descent on particles' positions (Lagrangian) is equivalent to an advection linear PDE on the density of particles (Eulerian). https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagrangian_and_Eulerian_specification_of_the_flow_field

title: Bicubic
content: Classic reference: R. Keys, Cubic convolution interpolation for digital image processing, 1980. Introduces bicubic interpolation, the most frequently used image interpolation method. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bicubic_interpolation

title: Planar Graphs
content: A graph is planar if and only if it does not contain as minor the complete graph K5 or the bipartite graph K33. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wagner%27s_theorem

title: Kl Gaussian
content: Classic reference: C. R. Rao, Information and the accuracy attainable in the estimation of statistical parameters, 1945. Introduces the Fisher-Rao which the canonical Riemannian metric associated to parametric families of densities. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fisher_information_metric

title: Richardson Lucy
content: Richardson-Lucy is the most celebrated deconvolution method under positivity constraints. https://en.m.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richardson%E2%80%93Lucy_deconvolution

title: Lic
content: Classic reference: B Cabral, L C Leedom, Imaging Vector Fields Using Line Integral Convolution, 1993. Line integral convolution is an anisotropic filtering which averages values along streamlines. Can be used for visualization of vector fields by diffusing noise. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Line_integral_convolution

title: Kmeans
content: K-means algorithm computes a stationary point of the quantization error by alternating between computation of Voronoi partition and computation of barycenters. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/K-means_clustering

title: Catmull Clark
content: Classic reference: E. Catmull, J. Clark, Recursively generated B-spline surfaces on arbitrary topological meshes, 1978. The most famous quad-mesh surface subdivision method. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Catmull%E2%80%93Clark_subdivision_surface

title: Netwon Fractal
content: Analyzing the global convergence of Newton is hard. Attraction basins are fractals whose boundaries are points which do not converge. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Newton_fractal

title: Normalized Cuts
content: Classic reference: J Shi and J Malik, Normalized Cuts and Image Segmentation, 2000. Splits a graph in two components by thresholding the Laplacian Fiedler vector. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spectral_clustering

title: Cas
content: The Hartley orthogonal matrix is associated to cas=cos+sin function. Defines an involutive real-valued Fourier-like transform. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Discrete_Hartley_transform

title: Fw
content: Classic reference: M Frank and P Wolfe, An algorithm for quadratic programming, 1956. F-W algorithm (also known as conditional gradient) optimizes functions on linear spaces by iteratively extracting extremal points of the constraints. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Frank%E2%80%93Wolfe_algorithm

title: Parabolic Pdes
content: Parabolic PDEs come with lots of flavors: heat, total variation, advection, Navier Stokes, etc. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Partial_differential_equation https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fluid_dynamics

title: Canny
content: Classic reference: J. Canny, A computational approach to edge detection, 1986. The most well-known edge detection method. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canny_edge_detector

title: Bezier
content: Bezier curve is barycentric interpolation using Bernstein polynomial weights. The most basic method for 2D CAD. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/B%C3%A9zier_curve https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bernstein_polynomial

title: Basis Pursuit
content: Classic reference: S Shaobing Chen, D L. Donoho, and M A. Saunders, Atomic Decomposition by Basis Pursuit, 1998, Introduces l1 regularization for signal decomposition. https://epubs.siam.org/doi/abs/10.1137/S1064827596304010

title: Nl Means
content: Non-local means compute an adaptive filtering by comparing patches in images. Started a whole field of research. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Non-local_means

title: Washall
content: Classic reference: S Warshall, A theorem on Boolean matrices, 1962. Robert Floyd, Algorithm 97: Shortest Path, 1962. Computes all pairs shortest paths in cubic time. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Floyd%E2%80%93Warshall_algorithm

title: Geodesic Woronoi
content: Voronoi diagram can be defined on surfaces using the geodesic distance. Dualize to a Delaunay triangulation of the surface. http://nbviewer.jupyter.org/github/gpeyre/numerical-tours/blob/master/matlab/fastmarching_4_mesh.ipynb https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Triangulation_(topology) https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Farth...

title: Bb Steps
content: Classic reference: J Barzilai, J Borwein, Two-Point Step Size Gradient Methods, 1988. B-B selects the step size for a gradient descent using a cheap approximation of the Hessian. Performs usually better than line search. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gradient_descent#Choosing_the_step_size_and_descent_direction

title: Subdiv
content: Subdivision surfaces define a hierarchy of embedded triangulations using simple refinement rules. At the heart of many successes in computer graphics and the movie industry. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Subdivision_surface http://nbviewer.jupyter.org/github/gpeyre/numerical-tours/blob/master/matlab/meshwav_2_subdiv...

title: Convnets
content: Classic reference: Y. LeCun, B. Boser, J. S. Denker, D. Henderson, R. E. Howard, W. Hubbard, L. D. Jackel, Backpropagation Applied to Handwritten Zip Code Recognition, 1989. Introduces convolutional neural networks trained by backpropagation. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Convolutional_neural_network

title: Vornoi Delaunay
content: The Delaunay triangulation is the dual of the Voronoi diagram. The most fundamental tool of computational geometry. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Delaunay_triangulation https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Voronoi_diagram https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Computational_geometry

title: Levelsets
content: Classic reference: S. Osher and J. A. Sethian, Fronts propagating with curvature-dependent speed: Algorithms based on Hamilton-Jacobi formulations, 1988. Lays out the foundations of the level set method for curve and surface evolutions. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Level-set_method

title: Dc Programming
content: Re-writing a non-convex optimization as a difference of convex (DC) leads to a simple iterative optimization method. Sometimes referred to as "convex-concave procedure" in the ML literature. http://www.lita.univ-lorraine.fr/~lethi/index.php/dca.html https://www.ceremade.dauphine.fr/~carlier/toland.pdf

title: Kringing
content: Classic reference: D.G Krige, A statistical approach to some mine valuations and allied problems at the Witwatersrand, 1951. Kriging (also known as Wiener interpolation) accounts for uncertainty in kernel interpolation using a Gaussian processes. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kriging

title: Tutte
content: Tutte embedding is the solution of a Poisson equation. Iterative resolution is equivalent to a system of masses and springs. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tutte_embedding http://nbviewer.jupyter.org/github/gpeyre/numerical-tours/blob/master/python/meshdeform_1_parameterization.ipynb

title: Cox
content: Classic reference: Maurice G. Cox, The Numerical Evaluation of B-Splines, 1972. Introduced (with De Boor) an efficient algorithm for the evaluation of B-splines, which revolutionized CAGD. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/De_Boor%27s_algorithm

title: Dykstra Pocs
content: POCS, Dykstra and DR often succeed in finding points in the intersection of possibly non-convex sets. Dykstra and DR usually work better. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Projections_onto_convex_sets https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dykstra%27s_projection_algorithm

title: Multipoles
content: Classic reference: L. Greengard and V. Rokhlin, A Fast Algorithm for Particle Simulations, 1987. Evaluates in O(n) in place of O(n^2) sums involving long-range interaction kernels. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fast_multipole_method

title: Maxcut
content: MAX-CUT is an NP hard problem. Goemans and Williamson SDP relaxation with randomized thresholding achieves a 0.879-approximation. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maximum_cut http://www-math.mit.edu/~goemans/PAPERS/maxcut-jacm.pdf

title: Qr
content: Classic reference: W. Givens, Computation of Plane Unitary Rotations Transforming a General Matrix to Triangular Form, 1958. The QR decomposition can be computed in a numerically stable way using planar rotation matrices. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Givens_rotation 25/12/2024 731-geodesic-voronoi.png Voronoi cells...

title: Optical Flow
content: Classic reference: B.K.P. Horn and B.G. Schunck, Determining optical flow, 1981. Computes optical flow by a quadratic regularization of the brightness constancy constraint. Solution is obtained by solving a linear system. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Horn%E2%80%93Schunck_method

title: Bernoulli
content: The Brachistochrone problem was solved by Bernoulli and is the birth of calculus of variations. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calculus_of_variations https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brachistochrone_curve

title: Chan Vese
content: Classic reference: T F. Chan, L. A. Vese, Active Contours Without Edges, 2001. The simplest yet most celebrated region-based segmentation method. Minimizes a binary Mumford-Shah segmentation functional using the level set method. https://www.ipol.im/pub/art/2012/g-cv/

title: Smacoff
content: SMACOF is the most popular stress minimization algorithm for multidimensional scaling (for dimensionality reduction or shape flattening). https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stress_majorization

title: Planar Graphs
content: Classic reference: K Wagner, Bemerkungen zum Vierfarbenproblem, 1936. Later improved by Komuro. Any pair of planar triangulations of n vertices can be connected by O(n) edge flips (despite the exponential number of such triangulations). https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flip_graph

title: Min Max
content: Min/max games are convex/concave saddle points. Can be solved by primal-dual algorithms. Converges to Dirac mass strategies only when K has a single saddle point, otherwise selects mixed strategies. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Minimax

title: Inpainting
content: Classic reference: JA. Criminisi; P. Perez; K. Toyama, Region filling and object removal by exemplar-based image inpainting, 2004. Introduces the idea of doing inpainting by pixel recopy. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inpainting

title: Edge Collapse
content: Edge collapse is a fundamental mesh processing primitive, at the heart of many mesh simplification methods. Influential papers by Hoppe, Garland and Heckbert. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Progressive_meshes

title: Stft
content: Classic reference: J Allen, Short Time Spectral Analysis, Synthesis, and Modification by Discrete Fourier Transform, 1977. Popularized the use of the spectrogram as the baseline tool for audio processing. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spectrogram https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Short-time_Fourier_transform

title: Grad Flow
content: The gradient field defines the steepest descent direction. The gradient flow dynamic defines a segmentation of the space into attraction basins of the local minimizers. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gradient https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gradient_descent

title: Poljak
content: Classic reference: B Poljak, Some methods of speeding up the convergence of iteration methods, 1964. Introduces momentum methods to speed up gradient descent schemes. https://distill.pub/2017/momentum/

title: Moreau Bregman
content: Moreau's decomposition generalizes the orthogonal decomposition to general functions. It can also be generalized beyond Euclidean space using Bregman divergences in place of Euclidean distance. https://hal.archives-ouvertes.fr/hal-01076974/document

title: Scale Space Filtering
content: Classic reference: A Witkin, Scale-space filtering, 1984. Introduces (with J. Koenderink) the notion of scale space, i.e., the multi-scales analysis of signals and images, which is at the heart of many vision architectures. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scale_space

title: Monotone Operator
content: Classic reference: R. Tyrrell Rockafellar, Monotone Operators and the Proximal Point Algorithm, 1976. The proximal point algorithm is the most fundamental non-smooth optimization method and is the basis for many other efficient proximal splitting methods (FB, DR, ADMM, Dykstra, etc). https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pr...

title: Lloyd
content: Optimal quantization solves a minimum Optimal Transport projection. Lloyd algorithm computes a stationary point of this non-convex energy (see work by Canas and Rosasco https://arxiv.org/pdf/1209.1077.pdf)

title: Sibson
content: Classic reference: R Sibson, A vector identity for the Dirichlet tessellation, 1980. Defines natural neighbor interpolation, generalizing piecewise linear interpolation to higher dimensions. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Natural_neighbor_interpolation

title: Hausdorff
content: The space of compact sets in a metric space is a compact set for the Hausdorff metric. Hausdorff convergence is weak and does not preserve topology, dimension, length, or path-connectedness. It preserves connectedness and convexity. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hausdorff_distance

title: Thin Plate
content: Classic reference: J. Duchon, Splines minimizing rotation invariant semi-norms in Sobolev spaces, 1976. Thin plate spline is one of the most popular data interpolation methods. Its solution can be written in 2D using the r^2 log(r) radial basis function. https://github.com/dill/duchon-typeset/blob/master/paper.pdf

title: Proj Grad
content: Projected gradient is the simplest algorithm to perform constrained optimization of a smooth function. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Subgradient_method#Projected_subgradient

title: Pendulum
content: Classic reference: C Huygens, Horologium Oscillatorium sive de motu pendulorum ad horologia aptato. Demonstrationes geometricae, 1673. First rigorous study of the motion of the pendulum (he also invented the pendulum clock), showing it is not isochronous. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pendulum_(mathematics)

title: N Ellipses
content: N-ellipses generalize ellipses with n foci. Spectrahedra (hence convex) algebraic curves of degree less than 2^n. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/N-ellipse https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spectrahedron

title: Cart
content: Classic reference: L. Breiman, J. H. Friedman, R. A. Olshen, and C. J. Stone. Classification and Regression Trees, 1984. Defines structured recursive classification and regression functions. Global optimization is achieved by dynamic programming. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Decision_tree_learning

title: Levelset
content: Interpolating between implicit equations defines morphings between curves or surfaces. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Implicit_surface#Metamorphoses_of_implicit_surfaces

title: Distance Reconstr
content: Classic reference: S F Gibson, Using distance maps for accurate surface reconstruction in sampled volumes, 1998. Dual contouring methods usually produce better quality meshes than primal ones. https://people.eecs.berkeley.edu/~jrs/meshpapers/SchaeferWarren2.pdf

title: Medial Axis
content: The medial axis (also known as skeleton) is the set of points where the distance is not smooth. Used as a shape descriptor in computer vision. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Medial_axis https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Topological_skeleton

title: Moreau
content: Classic reference: J-J Moreau, Proximite et dualite dans un espace hilbertien, 1965. Moreau-Yosida regularization smoothes a function by inf-convolution. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Convex_conjugate#Infimal_convolution

title: Qr Algo
content: QR algorithm is a gem of numerical algebra: iterative QR decomposition converges to a triangular matrix. Converges to a diagonal matrix for symmetric inputs. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/QR_algorithm

title: Kl
content: Classic reference: R. Leibler and S. Kullback, On information and sufficiency, 1951. KL divergence (also known as relative entropy) is a Bregman and Csiszar divergence between distributions and has an information-theoretic interpretation. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kullback%E2%80%93Leibler_divergence

title: Stable Fluids
content: Stable fluids of Jos Stam is a semi-Lagrangian solver for Navier-Stokes, which was very influential in graphics because of its simplicity and stability. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jos_Stam http://nbviewer.jupyter.org/github/gpeyre/numerical-tours/blob/master/python/graphics_5_fluids.ipynb

title: Gale Shapley
content: Classic reference: D Gale and L Shapley, College Admissions and the Stability of Marriage. The stable marriage is solved by the Gale-Shapley algorithm. Shapley and Roth got the Nobel prize in economics for this. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stable_marriage_problem

title: Quadratic Bezier
content: A quadratic bezier spline is the envelope of regularly spaced lines. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/B%C3%A9zier_curve

title: Wienner
content: Classic reference: N Wiener, Extrapolation, Interpolation, and Smoothing of Stationary Time Series, 1949. Introduces Wiener interpolation (also known as Kriging) and filtering, which founded with C. Shannon modern communication theory. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wiener_filter

title: Svm
content: Support vector machines maximize the classification margin for linear decision boundaries. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Support-vector_machine https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/VC_dimension

title: Marr
content: Classic reference: D. Marr and E. Hildreth, Theory of edge detection, 1980. Laid out the foundations of low-level edge detection. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edge_detection https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Marr_(neuroscientist)

title: Eigen Laplacian
content: Eigenvectors of the Laplacian on compact planar domains define an orthogonal basis of oscillating functions, which generalize Fourier sinusoids. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dirichlet_eigenvalue

title: Marching Cube
content: Classic reference: W Lorensen, H Cline, Marching Cubes: A high resolution 3D surface construction algorithm, 1987. The standard algorithm to extract iso-curves/surfaces from a discretized image/volume. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marching_squares https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marching_cubes

title: Shepard
content: Shepard interpolation generalizes nearest neighbor interpolation. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inverse_distance_weighting

title: Nesterov
content: Classic reference: Y Nesterov, A method for solving a convex programming problem with convergence rate O(1/k^2). Improves the 1/k rate of vanilla gradient descent to 1/k^2. https://blogs.princeton.edu/imabandit/2013/04/01/acceleratedgradientdescent/

title: Fench Rock
content: Fenchel-Rockafellar duality leverages linear operators in Lagrange duality. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fenchel%27s_duality_theorem https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Duality_(optimization)

title: Lotka
content: Classic reference: A. J. Lotka, Contribution to the Theory of Periodic Reaction, 1910. Lotka-Volterra is a non-linear ODE modeling chemical reaction or prey/predator behaviors which exhibits periodic solutions. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lotka%E2%80%93Volterra_equations

title: Barron
content: Multilayer perceptron with 1 hidden layer breaks the curse of dimensionality for Barron's functions. http://www.stat.yale.edu/~arb4/publications_files/UniversalApproximationBoundsForSuperpositionsOfASigmoidalFunction.pdf

title: Bertrand
content: Classic reference: J. Bertrand, Theoreme relatif au mouvement d'un point attire vers un centre fixe, 1873. Only harmonic spring and gravity central forces produce periodic motions. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bertrand%27s_theorem

title: Laplace Beltrami
content: Wave equation on a surface. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wave_equation

title: Radiosity
content: Classic reference: D Immel, M Cohen, D Greenberg, A radiosity method for non-diffuse environments, 1986. Describes conservation of light as an integral equation which is at the heart of global rendering techniques such as radiosity. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rendering_equation

title: Birkhoff
content: Birkhoff's contraction for Hilbert's metric is a key tool to quantify convergence of Markov-Chains (Perron-Frobenius). https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hilbert_metric

title: Metaballs
content: Classic reference: J Blinn, A Generalization of Algebraic Surface Drawing, 1982. "Metaballs" are levelsets of mixtures of radial basis functions, which generate blobby lava-lamp-like behaviors. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metaballs

title: Reaction Diffusion
content: Reaction-diffusion with spatially varyingg weights. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reaction%E2%80%93diffusion_system https://fr.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Chemical_Basis_of_Morphogenesis

title: Farthest Point
content: Classic reference: T Gonzalez, Clustering to minimize the maximum intercluster distance, 1985. Popularized the farthest point sampling greedy algorithm. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Farthest-first_traversal

title: Eikonal
content: The solution of the Eikonal equation is solved by advancing a front in the normal direction, similar to a grass fire. The most famous Hamilton-Jacobi equation. Refraction occurs when the speed has a discontinuity (Snell-Descart).

title: Spline Warping
content: Classic reference: R.L. Harder and R.N. Desmarais, Interpolation using surface splines, 1972. Thin plate (biharmonic) splines is a popular interpolation method with a closed form thanks to the theory of reproducing Hilbert spaces. Defines a Sobolev space of smooth functions. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thin_plate_...

title: Cats Bunny
content: Cats, bunnies, and elephants in graphics and applied maths.

title: Visual Cortex
content: Classic reference: D Hubel, T Wiesel, Receptive fields, binocular interaction and functional architecture in the cat's visual cortex, 1962. Describes the organisation of the visual cortex using oriented filters. Nobel prize in 1981. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=IOHayh06LJ4

title: Scale Space
content: Classic reference: J Koenderink, The structure of images, 1984. Introduces (with A. Witkin) the notion of scale space, i.e., the multi-scale analysis of signals and images, which is at the heart of many vision architectures. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scale_space

title: Laplacian Pyramid
content: The Laplacian pyramid is the ancestor of the wavelet transform. Defines a compact multiscale representation by iterative lowpass/highpass filterings. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pyramid_(image_processing)

title: Kruskal
content: Classic reference: J. B. Kruskal, On the shortest spanning subtree of a graph and the traveling salesman problem, 1956. Computes the minimum spanning tree in n log(n) operations. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prim%27s_algorithm

title: Optim
content: Optimization algorithms come with many flavors depending on the structure of the problem. Smooth vs non-smooth, convex vs non-convex, stochastic vs deterministic, etc. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mathematical_optimization

title: Multires Meshes
content: Classic reference: M Eck, T DeRose, T Duchamp, H Hoppe, M Lounsbery, W Stuetzle, Multiresolution analysis of arbitrary meshes, 1995. http://hhoppe.com/proj/mra/

title: Porous Medium
content: Nonlinearity matters. Linear diffusion (heat) has non-compactly supported solutions. Non-linear diffusion (porous medium) drives dynamics with compactly supported solutions. The porous medium is the simplest case, studied in detail by Otto. https://www.mis.mpg.de/preprints/1999/preprint1999_8.pdf

title: Multigrid
content: Classic reference: A. Brandt, Multi-Level Adaptive Solutions to Boundary-Value Problems, 1977. Introduces the multigrid method, which is the fundamental tool to speed up the convergence of low frequencies for the resolution of PDEs. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Multigrid_method

title: Pagerank
content: Page rank is the leading eigenvector of a stochastic matrix. Can be computed efficiently for sparse graphs using power iterations. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PageRank

title: Dykstra
content: Classic reference: J. P. Boyle and R. L. Dykstra, A method for finding projections onto the intersection of convex sets in Hilbert spaces, 1986. Dykstra's algorithm is the simplest method to project on the intersection of two convex sets. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dykstra%27s_projection_algorithm

title: Mirror Desc
content: Mirror descent generalizes gradient descent using Bregman geometries. https://blogs.princeton.edu/imabandit/2013/04/16/orf523-mirror-descent-part-iii/

title: Steiner
content: Classic reference: V. Jarnik, M. Kossler, On minimal graphs containing n given points, 1934. The Euclidean Steiner tree looks for the shortest irrigation tree of nodes. This paper proved the main property of this tree, which is hard to compute. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steiner_tree_problem

title: Laplace Legendre
content: The Laplace and the Legendre transforms are related by an exponential change of variables. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laplace_transform https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Legendre_transformation

title: Phase Retrieval
content: Classic reference: R. W. Gerchberg, W. O. Saxton, A practical algorithm for the determination of the phase from image and diffraction plane pictures, 1972. The simplest (but not the best) algorithm for phase retrieval. Computes iterative projections. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gerchberg%E2%80%93Saxton_algorithm

title: Cage Warps
content: Mean value coordinates extend usual barycentric coordinates to arbitrary polygons, including non-convex ones! Defined by Michael Floater in 2003. https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0167839603000025 http://nbviewer.jupyter.org/github/gpeyre/numerical-tours/blob/master/matlab/meshdeform_4_barycentric.i...

title: Ot Gaussians
content: 1D Optimal Transport distances between Gaussians is the Euclidean distance on the (mean, standard deviation) 2D plane. https://projecteuclid.org/euclid.ojm/1326291215

title: Dtw
content: Classic reference: H Sakoe and S Chiba, Dynamic programming algorithm optimization for spoken word recognition, 1978. Dynamic Time Warping aligns two time series by an increasing map. Solved in quadratic time by dynamic programming. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dynamic_time_warping

title: Gibbs Sampling
content: Gibbs distributions are maximum entropy distributions. Used in conjunction with MCMC methods to generate samples close to minimizers of the functional. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gibbs_measure https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Markov_chain_Monte_Carlo
